call.text: The routing module decides chunk boundaries by measuring cosine similarity between adjacent encoder outputs and converting the similarity into a boundary probability p_t that ranges from 0 to 1 [HNET:2.2.1:c023]. Specifically, it computes query and key vectors q_t = W_q \hat{x}_t and k_t = W_k \hat{x}_t, then sets p_t = ½ (1 − (q_t^⊤ k_{t‑1}) / ‖q_t‖‖k_{t‑1}‖) [HNET:2.2.1:c023]. A hard boundary indicator b_t is obtained by thresholding p_t at 0.5, i.e., b_t = 1 if p_t ≥ 0.5 and 0 otherwise, with p_1 defined as 1.0 to start the sequence with a boundary [HNET:2.2.1:c023]. This mechanism implements the intuition that lower similarity between consecutive vectors signals a contextual or semantic shift, prompting a boundary [HNET:1:c007]. The routing module thus dynamically draws chunk boundaries based on these similarity‑derived probabilities.
